text:
maria (support): Customer (tenant-abc) opened a ticket: sustained 429s on Dedicated pool quiet-pool-2 during a nightly ingest. They have reserved capacity but still getting throttled. Can infra take a look?

alexg (eng-infra): grabbing logs now. Do we have the tenant quota config they are on?

maria (support): pasted the admin export they shared: 
```
tenant_id: tenant-abc
quota:
  rate: 1000
  unit: minute
  scope: per_tenant
  model_caps: {}
```
They say they expected 1000 req/sec but admin UI shows 1000 "per minute" — looks off.

alexg (eng-infra): seeing a flood of 429s with reason=per_tenant_rate_limit in the middleware logs: 
```
[2026-10-03T03:12:01Z] pool=quiet-pool-2 req_id=... tenant=tenant-abc status=429 reason=per_tenant_rate_limit tokens=3500 unit=minute
[2026-10-03T03:12:03Z] pool=quiet-pool-2 req_id=... status=200 backend_latency=18ms
[2026-10-03T03:12:04Z] pool=quiet-pool-2 req_id=... status=429 reason=per_tenant_rate_limit tokens=3600 unit=minute
```
Pattern: big bursts of tokens all within a few seconds but quota checked as per_minute so it's tripping earlier than customer expected.

samr (dedicated-pm): interesting: autoscaler didn't spin up extra instances. Remember autoscaler triggers on pool queue depth and backend utilization. If the middleware rejects before queueing (rate limiter early-exit), the pool sees less queued work and doesn't scale — so throttling can happen without autoscale kicking in. That matches these logs.

maria (support): customer notes workload is embedding bulk jobs (large token counts per call) using a single long-lived connection. So high token throughput but limited concurrency -> noisy neighbor effect on token budget rather than connections.

alexg (eng-infra): repro steps I used: replayed 300 requests of ~10k tokens each at ~50 qps against a dedicated pool with tenant quota=1000/min. Result: many 429s within the first 20s, pool stayed at base size (no autoscale). Script: 
```
# quick replay
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -X POST "$REDWOOD_ENDPOINT/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"x","max_tokens":10000}'; sleep 0.02; done
```

ops-bot: alert auto: tenant=tenant-abc throttle_rate_exceeded=TRUE pool=quiet-pool-2

samr (dedicated-pm): mitigations: 
- short-term: bump tenant quota to match customer expectation (change unit to per_second equivalent).
- medium: adjust rate-limiter to count "token-rate" with same unit semantics used by billing (we currently have ambiguous unit names).
- long-term: expose burst tokens and soft caps in Console per-tenant + route high-token calls to a burstable path that still queues so autoscaler can react.

maria (support): I applied a temporary override for tenant-abc to 6000/min (via admin API) and the customer reports errors dropped to near 0. Command used: 
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/tenant-abc/quota" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate":6000, "unit":"minute"}'
```
Customer accepts this while we fix parsing/UX.

alexg (eng-infra): root cause: config ingestion allowed both "unit: minute" and "unit: per_minute" and elsewhere code expects "per_second" semantics for token buckets. We need a migration and stricter validation. I'll open a PR to normalize units and add an ingest-time guard.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=fix/quota-unit-normalize -> staging (CI green)

samr (dedicated-pm): follow-ups:
- alexg to push the normalization + migration script (target: 48h).
- infra to add metric: "rate_limiter_rejections_not_queued" and dashboard panel (priority-high).
- product/console: add unit label and tooltip to quota editor to reduce confusion.
- ops: retro with the customer and consider default soft-burst tokens for embedding-heavy workloads.

maria (support): assigning: alexg (owner), samr (owner for product follow-ups), maria (owner for customer comms). Will update ticket with workaround and ETA.

alexg (eng-infra): noted. PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/482 — includes migration + validation + a unit test that asserts that rate 1000 minute -> 16.66 rps conversion applied correctly.

maria (support): customer notified and will keep this thread updated if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

samr (dedicated-pm): closing the incident when deploy reaches prod and metric is live. Leaving this thread for trace.

maria (support): resolved for now (temporary quota bump), next steps tracked in PR and JIRA RED-1283.
